subject: Future Tech
title: The RepRap Movement
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The RepRap Movement.

hook.text: In 2005, Adrian Bowyer at Bath University had a wild idea: a 3D printer that could print copies of itself.

buildup.text: The RepRap project made all designs open-source. Anyone could download the plans and build their own printer at home.

discovery.text: RepRap slashed the cost of 3D printing from hundreds of thousands of dollars in industry to a few hundred for hobbyists.

twist.text: MakerBot, Prusa, and most affordable 3D printers trace their roots to RepRap designs and open-source philosophy.

climax.text: The maker movement exploded. Millions of hobbyists now design and print custom parts in garages and schools worldwide.

punchline.text: A printer that prints itself democratized manufacturing.

quiz.question: What was unique about the RepRap project?
options: It was a self-replicating open-source printer
